candidates.label: Roman Empire (city of Rome, representative point)
candidates.support: The Roman Empire's identity and extent are undisputed; Wikidata's coordinate for the empire is the city of Rome, its capital, a reasonable representative point for an empire-level record that has no single natural label position.

summary.text: The Roman Empire was the Mediterranean-wide state ruled from Rome. Its provinces and client kingdoms form the top of this project's 'about AD 50' hierarchy: every place in this dataset lay within one of its provinces during Paul's journeys. Augustus (formerly Octavian) became its first emperor after his victory over Mark Antony and Cleopatra at the Battle of Actium in 31 BC. Luke's Gospel sets Jesus' birth under a census decree from 'Caesar Augustus,' and Acts records that Paul, as a Roman citizen, exercised his right to 'appeal to Caesar.'

history.text: After defeating Mark Antony and Cleopatra at Actium in 31 BC, Octavian took the name Augustus and, in 27 BC, reorganized the Roman world into provinces he assigned to the Senate and provinces he retained for himself, the same broad division this project's 'about AD 50' provinces reflect.
At AD 50, the reigning emperor was Claudius (AD 41-54), who succeeded Augustus (27 BC-AD 14), Tiberius (AD 14-37) and Gaius 'Caligula' (AD 37-41).

scripture.textWEB: Now in those days, a decree went out from Caesar Augustus that all the world should be enrolled.

For if I have done wrong and have committed anything worthy of death, I don’t refuse to die; but if none of those things is true that they accuse me of, no one can give me up to them. I appeal to Caesar!”
